question: Should OpenClaw adopt agent-managed retrieval as a supported core capability, or require it to begin as an external skill/plugin built on current extension seams?
rationale: The request introduces a new orchestration model and potentially new runtime, tool, and cost-policy contracts; source-level repair automation cannot choose that product boundary safely.

options.title: Prototype outside core
options.body: Recommend a skill or plugin prototype that demonstrates retrieval quality, latency, token cost, and required APIs before any core commitment.

options.title: Sponsor core design
options.body: Accept this as core direction and assign an owner to define the agent, tool, security, budget, and compatibility contracts before implementation.

options.title: Decline for now
options.body: Keep the current retrieval model until a concrete OpenClaw user problem and missing extension seam are demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Prototype outside core
recommendation.body: Recommend a skill or plugin prototype that demonstrates retrieval quality, latency, token cost, and required APIs before any core commitment.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposer is the only identifiable participant in the supplied context and can refine the proposed boundary; maintainer sponsorship remains required.
